family: independent convex geometry and boundary adversary
independence: EARLY_SEAL.md was written before old proof, review, scripts, receipts, or sibling results were read
strongest_verified_result: A compact convex body in R3 with C^{2,alpha} boundary, 0<alpha<1, one globally constant area for all admissible tangent-inclusive strips of fixed positive width h, and h<2 inradius is a ball.
universal_geometric_findings: Admissible offsets are exactly [a(u), b(u)-h], including tangent endpoints
Nonempty open convex-boundary caps have positive surface area
Under 0<h<diameter and the global strip condition, minimum support width is strictly greater than h
The tetrahedron control has minimum width 2, inradius 1/sqrt(3), diameter 2sqrt(2); h=3/2 refutes the general inradius shortcut
Centered all-orientation admissibility is erosion by a ball of radius h/2; the open starting set exists exactly for h<2 inradius
The original nested-sphere example has area 13pi in all orientations and all admissible offsets
For two concentric spheres R>r>0 and 0<h<2R, strip area is constant exactly for h>=R+r, including threshold tangencies to the inner sphere
Fixed-width sliding integrals give finite-support a.e. periodic density, not constancy or a family of smaller widths
exact_remaining_gaps: h>=2 inradius within the intended convex positive fixed-width target
Removal of the C^{2,alpha} boundary hypothesis
All-direction compatibility is absent from a standalone periodic-density diagnostic
completion_estimate_scope: This assigned independent geometric audit, not the full Ghomi research goal
